column1: # The partial import record of the preserved historical Codex app-server trace
# It is derived from the ACTUAL frozen historical trace retained by the completed
# findings.tsv, world.tsv, prompt.txt) — the first completed pair of the
# 2026-10-08 paired cohort, produced by the `codex-app-server` backend, not by
# DSH. Only the fields that trace actually recorded are carried with a value;
# every field the trace does not contain is the literal `Unavailable` and is
# never fabricated. No native DSH session log, event stream, checkpoint or commit
# event is synthesized, because the preserved trace is an aggregate receipt and
# The one recorded artifact carried byte-for-byte is the trace's own prompt:
# `historical-codex-prompt.txt` is the exact 1787 bytes of the preserved
# `prompt.txt`, and its sha256 equals the recorded `promptIdentity` field below.
# The import verifies that equality before it publishes anything, so the recorded
# prompt is admitted only under its recorded hash.

column9: Non-interactive iOS API-key creation always fails here: appleApiKeyId is initialized to undefined and is neither declared in the options schema nor read from options. Even with all advertised flags supplied, the command uploads the key and then exits without creating a destination. Expose and consume an appleApiKeyId option.

The certificate password is collected with an ordinary text prompt, exposing it on screen and in terminal recordings or scrollback. The key-password prompt below and the app-specific-password prompt in destinations/create.ts have the same issue. Use masked input for these credentials.
